1501:
** εἴκοσι**
(for εἴκοσιν see below), _Attic dialect_, _Ionic dialect_, also {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus, “IG” 5(2).3.1 (from Tegea), and _Aeolic dialect_, [prev. work]12(2).6.21 (from Lesbos)}}:—_indeclinable_, **twenty**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.510, 748, etc.; in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus}} more frequently in _Epic dialect_ form **ἐείκοσι**, before a vowel ἐείκοσιν, {{Refs|1.309, 6.217, +others}}; _Doric dialect_ **ϝίκατι** {{Refs|“Leg.Gort.” 4.13, etc.}}; **ϝείκατι** {{Refs|“Tab.Heracl.” 2.71}}; _Laconian dialect_ **βείκατι** {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}; **εἴκατι** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|“IG” 9(1).693.10 (Corc.), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.10, 5.86. (Orig. ϝῑκατι and Εϝῑκοσι, whence ἐείκοσι in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus}}; ϝείκατι and εἴκατι are late spellings of (ϝ) ῑκατ; εἴκοσι is _contraction_ from *εϝῑκοσι. Cf. Latin _vīginti_, Sanskrit _viṃśatis._ εἴκοσιν is the only form used by {{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus, whether before vowels or consonants (εἴκοσ᾽ ἀπολογίζεται is uncertain in “fragment” 465); also (before consonants) 3rd c.BC: Herodas Mimographus 3.91, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “de Pietate - Herkulanische Studien” 3, etc., but not common in Inscrr. or Papyrus, e.g. (before consonants) “Schwyzer” 707 B 2 (Ephesus, 6th c.BC), “IG” 2.804.155 (4th c.BC), (before a vowel) “PGrenf.” 2.75.7 (4th c.AD)}}; εἴκοσι ἔτη, εἴκοσι ἡμερῶν, {{Refs|“IG” 12.94,49.)}}
1517:
** εἰρηνο-ποιέω**,
**to make peace**, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Pro.10.10, NT.Col.1.20, “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 2.203}}:—_middle_, **make peaceful**, [ψυχὴ] τὸν ἴδιον δρόμον -εῖται {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Hermes Trismegistus cited in 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes 1.49.45.}}
1526:
** εἰσί**,
_3rd.pers._ _plural_ of εἰμί (**sum**). **εἶσι**, _3rd.pers._ _singular_ of εἶμι (**ibo**). **εἰσῐδεῖν**, _Epic dialect_ εἰσιδέειν, _aorist_ _infinitive_ of εἰσεῖδο; see at {εἰσοράω}.
1528:
** εἰσκᾰλέω**,
**call in,** μάρτυρας {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 936, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 28.5; τινὰ πρὸς αὑτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.3.1, compare 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.132, “PPetr.” 2p.31 (3rd c.BC)}}, etc.:—_middle_, _invite to one's house, _{{NT|NT.Acts.10.23}}; also, **call** or **have called in,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.22.2}}; [ἰητρόν] {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “προγνωστικόν” 1}}; **summon,** {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|PPetr. 3p.62 (3rd c.AD).}}
1531:
** εἰσπορεύω**,
**lead in,** οἴκαδε {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 1285}}:—_passive_, **go into, enter,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.21, “UPZ” 6.30 (3rd c.BC)}}; εἰς τὸ ἄδυτον {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“OG” 156.4 (3rd c.BC)}}; πρός τινα {{NT|NT.Act.28.30. Used for εἰσέρχομαι in later Gr.,compare “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 91.}}
1532:
** εἰστρέχω**,
_aorist_ I _subjunctive_ εἰσθρέξωσιν {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Lycophron Tragicus 1163}}: _aorist 2_ **-έδρᾰμον**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.67, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 13.24}}: _perfect_ εἰσδεδράμηκα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Σαμία” 146}}:—**run in,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus [same place]}}; εἰσέδραμε Φᾶσιν, of a ship, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus}} [prev. cited]; ἡ θεὸς (i.e. ποδάγρα) διὰ ποδῶν εἰ. {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Ocyp.Praef.”}}
1539:
** ἑκάστοτε**,
_adverb_ **each time, on each occasion,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Parmenides Poeta Philosophus 16.1, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.90, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.4.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 393b; ἀεὶ..ἑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1280; ἑ. πολλάκις 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 58a}}; ἵνα ἑ. wherever **on each occasion,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.115.}}
1540:
** ἑκᾰτόν**,
{{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD(?): Arcadius Grammaticus}} **ἑκοτόν** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“IG” 5(2).3 (Tegea, 4th c.BC)}}, οἱ, αἱ, τά, _indeclinable_:— **a hundred,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.510, etc.}}: in compounds frequently loosely for **very many.** (Dissim. from **sém [kcirc]ṃtóm,** compare εἷς and Latin _centum,_ Lithuanian _ši[mtilde]tas,_ etc.)
1541:
** ἑκᾰτοντα-έτης**, ες,
**of a hundred years,** βιοτά {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.282; 100}} **years old,** {{LXX|LXX.Gen.17.17.}}
1542:
** ἑκᾰτοντα-πλᾰσίων**, ον,
_genitive_ ονος, **a hundred times as much** or **many,** with _genitive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 2.3}}: without _genitive_, **a hundredfold,** {{LXX+NT|LXX.2Ki.24.8; καρπός NT.Luke.8.8.}}
1543:
** ἑκᾰτόντ-αρχος**, ὁ,
={ἑκατοντάρχης}, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.3.41, NT.Matt.8.5, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.131, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lucullus” 35, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Tactica” 10.3.}}
1547:
Related to: ** ἐκγᾰμ-έομαι**,
_passive_, **to be given in marriage,** {{Refs|AB 259, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus}}
1548:
Related to: ** ἐκγᾰμ-έομαι**,
_passive_, **to be given in marriage,** {{Refs|AB 259, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus}}
1550:
** ἐκδᾰπᾰνάω**,
**exhaust,** χορηγίας {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 21.10.9; προσόδους [prev. author] 24.7.4, compare “PBaden” 19.19 (2nd c.AD)}}; τὸ αἷμα, τὸ ὑγρόν, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.192, 15.86: _metaphorically_, τὰς προθυμίας εἰς τοὺς ἐχθρούς 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 15.5.1; τὸν θυμὸν εἴς τινας 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Declamationes” 37.30}}:—_passive_, ἐκδεδαπανῆσθαι ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν {{NT|NT.2Cor.12.15.}}
1555:
** ἐκδιηγέομαι**,
**tell in detail,** {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Prog.” I, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1434b4, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.118, LXX.Job.12.8, etc.}}
1557:
** ἐκδῐκ-ησις**, εως, ἡ,
**avenging,** ἐ. ποιεῖσθαι to give **satisfaction,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.8.10}}; ἐ. ποιεῖσθαί τινος obtain it from.., {{Refs|“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2826 (from Aphrodisias)}}; **legal remedy,** {{Refs 6th c.AD+|PLond. 5.1674.102 (6th c.AD)}}; ἐ. ποιεῖν τινι **avenge** him, {{NT|NT.Act.7.24; τινός NT.Luke.18.7, 8.}}
1559:
** ἐκδῐ-ώκω**,
**chase away, banish,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.24; ἐκ τοῦ τόπου 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 618b12; τῆς οἰκίας 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Tim.” 10}}; **attack, persecute,** {{Refs 6th c.AD+|PMasp. 2 iii4 (6th c.AD)}}, etc.:—_passive_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “Fragmenta” 238.}}
1573:
** ἐκκᾰκέω**,
**to be faint-hearted, lose heart, grow weary,** variant for{ἐγκ-}, {{NT|NT.Luke.18.1, NT.2Cor.4.1, 16, +others, cf. Vett. Val. 201.15, “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”}}
1579:
** ἐκκολυμβάω**,
**plunge into the sea from..,** with _genitive_, ναός {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1609: _absolutely_, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 80, compare 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 20.86, NT.Act.27.42}}; **swim ashore,** εἰς τὴν γῆν {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 5.24, compare 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Συριακή” 6.}}
1583:
** ἐκλᾰλ-έω**,
**blurt out, blab, divulge,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.26, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.64, +others, 5th-6th c.AD: Aeneas Gazaeus Rhetor “Epistulae” 7; τὸ ἐκλαλοῦν}}**talkativeness,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 219}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ὅρκος” 1, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 18.213.}}
1592:
** ἐκμυκτηρ-ίζω**,
**hold in derision, mock at,** {{LXX+NT|LXX.Psa.2.4, NT.Luke.16.14.}}
1597:
** ἔκπᾰλαι**,
_adverb_ for ἐκ πάλαι, **for a long time,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.323, NT.2Pet.3.5, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 16.8.4, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.548d, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 6.4.14, “POxy.” 938.3 (3rd-4th c.AD), etc.}}
